newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian GAZ carmaker to tap intl markets in autumn.
newsitem.headline: Russian GAZ carmaker to tap intl markets in autumn.

text.p: Russia's AO GAZ carmaker plans to make its debut on international financial markets this autumn with a Eurobond or share issue, President Nikolai Pugin said on Wednesday.

"We are actively involved with a partner in preparing an issue on international markets," he told Reuters. "This will be in the second half of the year, in the autumn. It is likely to be Eurobonds or our shares."

Pugin said that the carmaker's output plans for the year were on track. "We are planning a 14 percent rise in production and a 15 percent rise in sales compared to last year," he said at the opening of a showroom. "I think we will stick to this."
Gaz produced 209,141 vehicles in 1996 after 200,292 in 1995. Its chief product is Volga sedans, although its GAZelle light truck is proving extremely popular.

"Last year we had a profit," Pugin added. "This year the profit will be greater than last year." GAZ pre-tax profit to Russian accounting standards on an accruals basis was 735.6 billion roubles ($130 million) in 1996 after 1.44 trillion roubles in 1995 and net profit was 48.1 billion roubles after 44.8 billion.

Pugin said GAZ, located in Nizhny Novgorod 400 km (250 miles) east of Moscow, had chosen Credit Suisse as financial partner on the issue and would hire another firm in the next two or three months to improve its credit image.
